scope: Local change to the runtime grant script for the three new offline extensions: the QR-3 comparison tables, the QR-4 selection tables (including the four S2-2 tables, which do not exist yet) and the multi-Pine member-set tables join the insert-only list (SELECT and INSERT only for the runtime role), and their three markers join the read-only list. Both grant tests install every extension and assert the new lists. No grant is applied to any environment.
method: One integration coder (Sonnet 5.5) was the only writer of the grant script and its two tests, after the three extension coders returned their exact entries; check logic was not changed. A sole-runner tester then ran, with nothing else active, test/postgres/runtime-grants.test.mjs and every new extension file one file per process on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (fail 0 and skipped 0 in each), the install, inspect and rollback sequence of all three new tools with the repo grant script, test/postgres-runtime-grants.test.js and the full unit suite (2115 tests, 0 fail, 6 skipped, 9 todo). Root reviewed the diff.
hashNote: SHA-256 of the line-feed content as Git stores it.
result: test/postgres/runtime-grants.test.mjs 1 of 1 and test/postgres-runtime-grants.test.js 1 of 1 pass; every extension inspect with a role granted by this script reports no failures.
limits: The QR-3 S2c-2 tables are not in the lists yet; they are added when they exist.
The script is applied to no environment; a staging reapply belongs to the data-model window with a fresh owner GO.

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the diff and the verification and accepted the grant change as local engineering evidence. It grants nothing in any environment.
